title: Vortex lattices in coupled one-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensates with a synthetic magnetic field
authors: Holly A. J. Middleton-Spencer, Rose Davies, David G. Reid, Anna Dalmasso, Theodore Kazanas, Hannah M. Price
abstract: We investigate the mean-field ground states of coupled one-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensates subject to a synthetic magnetic field. The resulting interacting coupled-wire model has one continuous and one discrete spatial direction, providing a controlled way to interpolate between the physics of few-leg ladders and extended vortex lattices. For two wires, we study the vortex-like, biased-density, and Meissner-like states, exploring how the finite longitudinal size of the system modifies the transitions between them. Increasing the number of wires, the ground state evolves towards an extended vortex lattice. We find numerically that periodic boundary conditions in the discrete direction can favour staggered arrays of like-signed vortices resembling an Abrikosov lattice, while open boundaries in small finite-size systems confine the vortices into rows near the centre of the synthetic direction. Our results explore how finite size effects and boundary conditions govern the emergence and spatial organisation of vortices in continuous-discrete quantum fluids, with relevance to future experiments in tunnel-coupled atomic wires or with synthetic dimensions.
summary: This paper theoretically examines how vortex lattices form in coupled 1D Bose-Einstein condensates subjected to a synthetic magnetic field. By analyzing the mean-field ground states, the authors show that the resulting vortex structure is critically governed by whether the system boundaries are periodic or open. The findings provide crucial insights into controlling quantum fluid behavior in engineered atomic potentials.
main_problem: The study investigates the mean-field ground states of coupled one-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensates subjected to a synthetic magnetic field.
main_result: The system's vortex structure is highly dependent on boundary conditions, favoring Abrikosov-like lattices under periodic boundary conditions and confining vortices centrally under open boundary conditions.
method: The analysis employs mean-field theory, solving coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations using numerical methods like imaginary time evolution and variational ansatz.
model_or_system: The model is a coupled-wire system of 1D BECs, characterized by one continuous and one discrete spatial direction, allowing interpolation between few-leg ladders and extended vortex lattices.

important_parameters: Synthetic magnetic flux ($\phi$), inter-wire hopping strength ($J$), and the boundary conditions (Periodic vs. Open) in the discrete direction.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field approximations, treating the system as a bosonic condensate described by coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by first analyzing the non-interacting model, then developing the mean-field coupled-wire model, and finally comparing the resulting vortex states and ground state evolution under different boundary conditions.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the interplay between topology (synthetic fields), geometry (finite size/boundary conditions), and superfluidity in ultracold atomic systems, which is a major frontier in AMO physics.
